newsitem.title: ITALY: Ten Italians kidnapped in Yemen-Foreign Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ten Italians kidnapped in Yemen-Foreign Ministry.

text.p: Ten Italians have been abducted in two incidents in the north and south of Yemen, the Italian Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.
Earlier reports from security and diplomatic sources in the Yemeni capital Sanaa had said at least five European tourists, either Germans or Italians, had been kidnapped by tribesmen.

A Foreign Ministry official said a first group of six people was kidnapped in the south of the country on Wednesday afternoon while on their way to Al Mukallaa on the Gulf of Aden coast. He said they had been taken to the interior of the country.
"We have spoken to one of them and they are well, they are being treated well," he told Reuters. That group consisted of one family with a nine-year-old son and another with a daughter.
The official said four more Italians were kidnapped near Khamir, some 100 km (60 miles) north of Sanaa, on Thursday morning, but he had no further details.

The incident was the third of its kind in recent weeks. An Italian kidnapped by tribesmen earlier in August was released last Sunday after several days and two other Italian tourists were abducted in late July and freed after one day.
